title: Conormal fibres commute with an extension of the ground field
statement:
Let $k\to K$ be an extension of fields, let $C$ be a finite type commutative $k$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra], and choose a presentation $P=k[x_1,\ldots,x_n]\twoheadrightarrow C$ with kernel $I$ [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring]. Put $P_K=K[x_1,\ldots,x_n]$, let $I_K\subseteq P_K$ be the ideal generated by the coefficientwise images of $I$, and identify $C_K=K\otimes_k C$ with $P_K/I_K$ [lem-weil-pbc-presentation-base-change]. Let $\mathfrak q_K\subset C_K$ be prime, let $\mathfrak q$ be its inverse image in $C$, and let $\mathfrak q'$ and $\mathfrak q_K'$ be their inverse images in $P$ and $P_K$. Then the coefficient-extension map induces a canonical isomorphism of $\kappa(\mathfrak q_K)$-vector spaces
$$
 (I/I^2)_{\mathfrak q}\otimes_{C_{\mathfrak q}}\kappa(\mathfrak q)\otimes_{\kappa(\mathfrak q)}\kappa(\mathfrak q_K)\;\xrightarrow{\sim}\;(I_K/I_K^2)_{\mathfrak q_K}\otimes_{(C_K)_{\mathfrak q_K}}\kappa(\mathfrak q_K),
$$
where $\kappa(\mathfrak q)\to\kappa(\mathfrak q_K)$ is induced by $C\to C_K$, and the map sends $(f\bmod I^2)\otimes\lambda$ to $\lambda$ times the coefficientwise image of $f$ modulo $I_K^2$. In particular, the two vector spaces have the same finite dimension.

source.place: Tag 00SI (lemma-lci-field-change-local), proof lines 36215--36259: the displayed conormal-fibre identity and the application of Nakayama.

proof.text: Put $M=I/I^2$, $N=I_K/I_K^2$, and let $\gamma:P\to P_K$ be coefficient extension. Applying [lem-weil-pbc-presentation-base-change] to the identity presentation $P\to P$ (no relations) and swapping the tensor factors gives a $P$-algebra isomorphism $P\otimes_k K\simeq P_K$ sending $p\otimes\lambda$ to $\lambda\gamma(p)$. Its inverse sends $x_i$ to $x_i\otimes1$ and a coefficient $\lambda$ to $1\otimes\lambda$; the two composites fix coefficients and variables, hence are identities by [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring]. For the original quotient presentation, the identification $C_K=P_K/I_K$ in the statement is compatible with $C\to C_K$ and $\gamma$ on generators.

source.place: Tag 00SI (lemma-lci-field-change-local), first proof paragraph, polynomial presentations; Tag 05G3 base change.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-field-extension-base-change-faithfully-flat] to $k\to K$ and $D=P$. It makes $P\to P\otimes_k K$ faithfully flat, and hence flat by [def-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-ring-map]. Under the $P$-algebra isomorphism of step 1 this is $\gamma:P\to P_K$. Thus the flat hypothesis needed for conormal base change holds for this very coefficient-extension map.

source.place: Tag 00SI, $I_K=K\otimes_k I$; flat field extension and base change, Tags 00HB and 00HI.

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-ideal-cotangent-flat-base-change-ring] with $A=P$, $B=P_K$, and $J=I_K$, the map $\phi:M\otimes_P P_K\to N$, $[f]\otimes b\mapsto b[\gamma(f)]$, is an isomorphism. It is $P_K$-linear. Both modules are annihilated by $I_K$, so it is also $C_K$-linear: if $i\in I$ then $m\otimes\gamma(i)b=(im)\otimes b=0$. There is a canonical isomorphism $M\otimes_C C_K\to M\otimes_P P_K$ sending $m\otimes[b]$ to $m\otimes b$. It is well defined because every element of $I_K$ is a sum of multiples of images of elements of $I$, which annihilate the latter tensor product as just checked. Its inverse is $m\otimes b\mapsto m\otimes[b]$; balancing over $C=P/I$ follows by lifting a scalar to $P$. The two composites are the identity on pure tensors by [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. Compose to get $\Theta:M\otimes_C C_K\simeq N$, with $\Theta([f]\otimes[b])=b[\gamma(f)]$.

source.place: Tag 0473 (lemma-conormal-functorial-flat), affine proof; this supplies the conormal identity used in Tag 00SI and explicitly stated in Tag 00SJ.

proof.text: Write $F=\kappa(\mathfrak q)$ and $L=\kappa(\mathfrak q_K)$. The composite $C\to C_K\to L$ kills $\mathfrak q$ and takes $s\notin\mathfrak q$ to a nonzero element of $L$, since $\mathfrak q$ is the contraction of $\mathfrak q_K$. It therefore gives the map $C_{\mathfrak q}\to L$, $c/s\mapsto\bar c/\bar s$, killing $\mathfrak q C_{\mathfrak q}$, and hence a unital field map $F\to L$ by [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]. This field map is injective: its kernel is an ideal in the field $F$ and cannot contain $1$. These are exactly the residue-field structures in the statement.

source.place: Tag 00SI, corresponding primes and residue-field maps in the displayed identity; localization/residue fields as in Tags 00CO and 07BH.

proof.text: The fraction and tensor relations [def-weil-pbc-module-localization, def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product] give the canonical isomorphisms $M_{\mathfrak q}\otimes_{C_{\mathfrak q}}F\simeq M\otimes_C F$ and $N_{\mathfrak q_K}\otimes_{(C_K)_{\mathfrak q_K}}L\simeq N\otimes_{C_K}L$. In the first case the forward map is $(m/s)\otimes a\mapsto m\otimes(a/\bar s)$ and the inverse is $m\otimes a\mapsto(m/1)\otimes a$; in the second case use the same formulas with $C_K,N,L$. Fractions have equal images because an annihilating denominator becomes invertible in the residue field. The tensor balancing relations hold by multiplication of the displayed scalars, and the composites are identities since $(m/s)\otimes a=(m/1)\otimes(a/\bar s)$. Thus these identifications are proved directly for the modules at hand.

source.place: Tag 00SI, displayed tensor fibre identity; explicit fractions as in module localization Tag 07JZ and tensor-localization Tag 00DK.

proof.text: Tensor balancing also gives $ (M\otimes_C F)\otimes_F L\simeq M\otimes_C L$, $(m\otimes a)\otimes\lambda\mapsto m\otimes a\lambda$, with inverse $m\otimes\lambda\mapsto(m\otimes1)\otimes\lambda$. Likewise $(M\otimes_C C_K)\otimes_{C_K}L\simeq M\otimes_C L$ sends $(m\otimes b)\otimes\lambda$ to $m\otimes\bar b\lambda$ and has inverse $m\otimes\lambda\mapsto(m\otimes1)\otimes\lambda$. Each pair is inverse on pure tensors and respects the scalar relations [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. Tensoring $\Theta$ from step 3 with $L$ has inverse obtained by tensoring $\Theta^{-1}$. Compose these maps and the maps of step 5 to obtain the asserted $L$-linear isomorphism. On $([f]/1\otimes1)\otimes\lambda$ it gives $([\gamma(f)]/1)\otimes\lambda$, so it is precisely the canonical coefficient-extension map, with all denominators governed by step 5.

source.place: Tag 00SI, displayed equalities in the conormal-fibre calculation; Tag 00SJ, conormal identity $I\prime/(I\prime)^2=(I/I^2)\otimes_C C_K$.

proof.text: The ring $P$ is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-polynomial-ring-field-regular-ring], so $I=(f_1,\ldots,f_r)$ for some finite family by [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. Their classes generate $M$ over $C$: write any $f\in I$ as $\sum p_i f_i$ and reduce each $p_i$ modulo $I$. Hence their localized classes generate $M_{\mathfrak q}$, and their residue classes span $V=M_{\mathfrak q}\otimes_{C_{\mathfrak q}}F$. In particular $V$ is finite dimensional.

source.place: Tag 00SI, final comparison of finite generator numbers; Noetherian polynomial ring Tag 00OQ and definition Tag 00FM.

proof.text: Select a basis $v_1,\ldots,v_d$ of $V$ from the finite spanning family of step 7 by repeatedly discarding a vector in the span of the others. The vectors $v_i\otimes1$ span $V\otimes_F L$. They are independent: the coordinate functionals $\ell_j:V\to F$ extend by $v\otimes\lambda\mapsto\ell_j(v)\lambda$ to $L$-linear maps [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product], and applying the $j$th map to $\sum a_i(v_i\otimes1)=0$ gives $a_j=0$. Thus extension of scalars preserves $d$, including $d=0$. Step 6 identifies $V\otimes_F L$ with the right conormal fibre, proving the finite-dimension conclusion over the respective residue fields.

source.place: Tag 00SI, equality of residue-field dimensions following the displayed isomorphism.
